bib.title: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models", Shi, Ajith, Xia, Huang, Liu, Blevins, Chen, Zettlemoyer. Venue as printed: "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024" (arXiv:2310.16789v3, 9 Mar 2024). First author Weijia Shi: University of Washington; co-first author Anirudh Ajith: Princeton University.

COVERAGE: 23 of 23 pages extracted (80,314 chars). Pages 1-13 and appendices 19-23 read in full; reference pages 17-18 read; reference pages 14-16 skimmed (opening lines only). Figure plots are not in the text extraction, so the per-point values in Figures 2, 4, 5 and 7 are unread.

CLAIMS
- claim: Min-K% Prob is the average log-likelihood of the k% lowest-probability tokens; a higher score means member.
  number: k = 20
  setup: k swept over 10-50 on a held-out validation set with one LLaMA model, then fixed for all experiments
  quote: "MIN-K% P ROB(x) = 1E Xxi∈Min-K%(x) log p(xi|x1, ..., xi−1). (1) where E is the size of the Min-K%(x) set" and "found that k = 20works best. We use this value for all experiments without further tuning."
  where: p4, p5
- claim: It needs per-token probabilities but no reference model and no knowledge of the training corpus.
  number: none
  quote: "assuming that the detector has access to the LM only as a black box, and can compute token probabilities for any data point x"
  where: p3
- claim: WikiMIA is 394 member plus 394 non-member Wikipedia event pages, split by date.
  number: non-members created after 1 January 2023; members pre-2017 (also printed as pre-2016); truncated to 32, 64, 128, 256; original and ChatGPT-paraphrased settings
  quote: "we ultimately collected 394 recent events as our non-member data, and we randomly selected 394 events from pre-2016 Wikipedia pages as our member data"
  where: p4
- claim: Headline average AUC is 0.72 against 0.67 for the best baseline, perplexity.
  number: 0.72 vs 0.67. Per-model original-setting AUC: Pythia-2.8B 0.67, NeoX-20B 0.76, LLaMA-30B 0.74, LLaMA-65B 0.74, OPT-66B 0.71. Other baseline averages: Neighbor 0.65, Zlib 0.65, Lowercase 0.61, Smaller Ref 0.66.
  setup: WikiMIA, five open models, original and paraphrase settings
  quote: "MIN-K% P ROB achieves an AUC score of 0.72 on average, marking a 7.4% improvement over the best baseline method (i.e., PPL)"
  where: p5, Table 1 p6
- claim: At a 5% false-positive rate it catches only about a fifth of members.
  number: TPR@5%FPR average 22.2 (Zlib 20.6, PPL 19.3)
  setup: WikiMIA, same five models
  quote: "MIN-K% PROB 13.7 15.1 21.6 27.3 22.3 25.9 20.9 30.9 21.6 23.0 22.2"
  where: Table 6, p19
- claim: Downstream contamination, simulated: average AUC 0.86 against 0.84 for perplexity.
  number: BoolQ 0.91, Commonsense QA 0.80, IMDB 0.98, Truthful QA 0.74; TPR@5%FPR average 46 vs 42
  setup: LLaMA-7B further trained one epoch at learning rate 1e-4 on RedPajama text with 200 inserted and 200 held-out examples per dataset; 27M tokens, 0.1% contaminant
  quote: "MIN-K% P ROB 0.91 0.80 0.98 0.74 0.86"
  where: p8, Table 3; Table 7 p19
- claim: A lower learning rate makes detection much harder.
  number: at 1e-5: 0.64, 0.59, 0.76, 0.72, 0.56; at 1e-4: 0.91, 0.80, 0.98, 0.82, 0.74
  setup: same simulation; columns BoolQ, Commonsense QA, IMDB, LSAT QA, Truthful QA
  quote: "1 × 10−5 0.64 0.59 0.76 0.72 0.56"
  where: Table 4, p9
- claim: Detection gets easier with larger models, longer text and more occurrences; the effect of corpus size depends on whether the contaminant is an outlier.
  number: none in the text (plots only)
  setup: LLaMA 7/13/30/65B at length 128; lengths 32-256; Poisson-distributed duplicates; corpora of 0.17M-26M tokens (outlier) and 0.77M-7.6M (in-distribution news)
  quote: "Detection of outlier contaminants like downstream examples gets easier as data size increases ... detecting general in-distribution samples from the pretraining data distribution gets harder with more data"
  where: p5-6, p8
- claim: Copyrighted books: AUC 0.88 on the validation set, perplexity 0.84.
  number: 0.88; "nearly 90%" of 100 Books3 books flagged at over 50% contamination
  setup: text-davinci-003; validation set of 50 books believed memorised plus 50 books first published in 2023, 100 snippets of 512 words each; threshold chosen to maximise validation accuracy
  quote: "Figure 4 reveals nearly 90% of the books have an alarming contamination rate over 50%."
  where: p6-7
- claim: Unlearning audit: the "unlearned" Harry Potter model still reproduces content.
  number: 188 suspicious chunks of about 1000; 5.3% of completions scored 4 or above by GPT-4; 103 of 1000 questions selected, ROUGE-L recall 0.23 vs 0.10 for unselected
  setup: LLaMA2-7B-WhoIsHarryPotter vs LLaMA2-7B-chat, books 1-4, score ratio within (1/1.15, 1.15), 20 samples each
  quote: "Among the 103 selected questions, we observe an average ROUGE-L recall of 0.23. Conversely, for the unselected questions, the average ROUGE-L recall is 0.10."
  where: p10-12

LIMITS
- No limitations section. The headline is AUC, so no threshold is given for WikiMIA: "we don't need to determine the threshold ϵ" (p5). The only fitted threshold is the book one, and its value is not printed.
- No false-positive rate is reported for the book test set. All 100 test books are presumed positives, so the "nearly 90%" figure has no negative control beyond the validation set.
- Member and non-member sets differ in date as well as membership (pre-2017 vs 2023 events). The paper does not test whether the detector is picking up the date shift rather than membership.
- Book-validation positives are "likely" members, not confirmed.
- Contamination results come from a small fine-tuning simulation where inserted examples are outliers, not from real pretraining. The 1e-5 row shows near-chance AUC on some tasks.
- Closed models are covered only by text-davinci-003, which exposed log-probabilities. Models without token probabilities are out of scope.
- The 7.4% is relative (0.72 vs 0.67), about 5 AUC points.
- No confidence intervals or seeds anywhere.

BUILDS ON: Shokri et al. (2016) for membership inference; Yeom et al. (2018a) LOSS attack; Carlini et al. (2021) Zlib, Lowercase and smaller-reference attacks; Mattern et al. (2023) neighbourhood attack; Carlini et al. (2022) and Watson et al. (2022) reference-model calibration; Hardt et al. (2016) and Bassily et al. (2020) for the stability bound; Chang et al. (2023) for memorised books; Eldan & Russinovich (2023) for the unlearned model.

CODE: Algorithm 1, p23: "Select the top k% of tokens from x with the lowest probability and add to Min-k%(x)" then "If MIN-K% P ROB(x) > ϵ: return Non-member Else: return Member". Note this uses a sum of negative log-probabilities, the opposite sign and no 1/E compared with Eq. 1.

FIGURES: Figure 1, p2, "Overview of MIN-K% PROB": shows the per-token probability, bottom-k% selection and averaging steps in one picture. (Figure 2, p6, is the alternative for the size and length trends.)

PROBLEMS
- Internal inconsistencies in the source: members "created before 2017" vs "pre-2016"; k tuned on "LLAMA-60B" though only 65B is evaluated; corpus "27 million tokens" vs "26M"; LSAT QA appears in Tables 4 and 8 but not in the setup; Algorithm 1 is cited as Appendix B but sits in Appendix C; the conclusion says "two case studies" where the paper has three.
- Eq. 1 extraction dropped the fraction and summation symbols ("1E X" is 1/E times a sum); "( 11.15 , 1.15)" is (1/1.15, 1.15).
- Table 9 (p20) contains a GPT-4 judge prompt ("You are a helpful assistant..."). It is the paper's own evaluation template; I treated it as data and did not act on it.
